summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg (1889–1974) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908, taught at Fjellstedt School (c. 1916–1919), and served as lecturer and professor at Uppsala University (c. 1919–1956).
Henrik Zilliacus (1908–1992) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki from around 1926 to 1936 and held a post there from circa 1944 to 1975.

Henry Beveridge (1837–1929) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (c. 1853–1857) and Queen's University Belfast (1856), later serving in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and as President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Chung-hung Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto in 2006, having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren (1854–1899) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Harvard Oriental Series in 1891. He studied at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, working under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids.

Henry Creswicke Rawlinson (1810–1895) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. Educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, he held posts at the East India Company, the Foreign Office, and the University of London.

Henry George Keene (1781–1864) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, he served with the East India Company and as Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College.

Henry Hamilton Hadley (1826–1864) worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Yale, Union Theological Seminary, and Andover Theological Seminary, later holding Hebrew professorships and instructorships at Union Theological Seminary and Yale Divinity School.

Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS.

Henry Hoenigswald (1915–2003) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence between 1932 and 1937, and later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1985.

Henry Martyn (1781–1812) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College, and studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.
Henry Miers Elliot (1808–1853) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Winchester College and served as a civil servant with the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1783 to 1815, worked for the East India Company, and was Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.
Henry Steel Olcott (1832–1907) was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University from circa 1847 to 1849 and founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Heinrich Blochmann and served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William from circa 1870 to 1892.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837), an Indologist who studied under Citrapati, served the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College, and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society, which he co-founded.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty is an Indologist who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He served as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

Herbert Cushing Tolman (1865–1923) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale, Peabody College, and other institutions, later holding posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, North Carolina, and Vanderbilt University.

Herbert Franke (1914–2011) was a sinologist who studied under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer at Cologne, Bonn, and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Cologne, University of Munich, and served as President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Herbert Hope Risley (1851–1911) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Winchester College from circa 1863 to 1869 and at New College from circa 1869 to 1873.
